chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sad ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Abu Hafs Amr ibn Khalid narrated to me from his brother Sufyan ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever seeks forgiveness from God, the Mighty and Majestic, seventy times after Asr, God forgives seven hundred sins for him that day. If he does not have any, then for his father. If his father does not have any, then for his mother. If his mother does not have any, then for his brother. If his brother does not have any, then for his sister. If his sister does not have any, then for the nearest relative, then the next nearest.

key_terms.استغفار: Istighfar - seeking forgiveness from God, typically by saying 'astaghfirullah'
key_terms.العصر: Asr - the afternoon prayer, the third of the five daily prayers
key_terms.ذنب: Dhanb - sin, transgression against God's commands

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for seeking forgiveness seventy times after Asr prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that repeating istighfar (seeking God's forgiveness) seventy times after the Asr (afternoon) prayer results in God forgiving seven hundred sins. Remarkably, if the person has no sins remaining, the benefit cascades through their family hierarchy: father, mother, brother, sister, and then nearest relatives. This hadith highlights the immense spiritual reward of post-prayer istighfar and the interconnected spiritual welfare of family members in Islamic teaching.
